boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named TCU places for studying, making, gathering, moving, and taking part in campus life.

cards.title: Campus Commons
cards.subtitle: Central lawn by the BLUU and Frog Fountain
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or use the seating for a conversation, a quiet outdoor work session, or a campus event; check the calendar before planning around programming.
cards.short_summary: A central green for informal outdoor time and scheduled campus activity.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU describes Campus Commons as a landscaped open space with seating where students gather, study, hang out, and attend activities.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; events and setups can affect availability.

cards.title: Frog Fountain
cards.subtitle: Campus Commons
cards.notes: Use the fountain as a clear meet-up landmark, then take in the four lotus forms and their class-year symbolism from the surrounding plaza.
cards.short_summary: TCU’s four-plume fountain and a focal point within Campus Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU identifies Frog Fountain as a campus icon and location for student gatherings; its four flutes represent student classes.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark in Campus Commons; respect any event setup in the area.

cards.title: Brown-Lupton University Union (BLUU)
cards.subtitle: 2901 Stadium Drive
cards.notes: Stop in to orient yourself to dining, student-service offices, and the events calendar; use the building’s posted hours before making it a late study stop.
cards.short_summary: The campus union combines dining, services, and event space at the edge of Campus Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU says the BLUU houses its primary residential dining facility, retail options, student-services offices, and event facilities.
cards.access_notes: TCU lists building hours; some offices, dining venues, and events have separate schedules.

cards.title: Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.subtitle: Main campus library
cards.notes: Choose a floor to match the task: active lounges and café below, collaborative study on level two, or quieter reading and collections work upstairs.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor library with distinct quiet, collaborative, and technology-focused areas.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU documents active lounges on the ground level, collaboration and study spaces on the second floor, and quieter upper-level collections and lounges.
cards.source_title: History of the Library | Celebrating 100 Years of the Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.access_notes: Check current library hours and access guidance before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Mary Couts Burnett Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.notes: Reserve a room when your group needs to talk through a project, then use the library’s room-location map to find the assigned study area.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group work spaces distributed through the library.
cards.evidence_claim: The TCU Library provides maps for group study-room locations and identifies reservable group study rooms among its study options.
cards.source_title: Building maps, locations and directions | TCU Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.access_notes: Reservations and library access rules apply; consult the library’s current booking information.

cards.title: Fab Lab
cards.subtitle: First floor, Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.notes: Plan a hands-on project around the listed equipment, then make any needed equipment reservation before you arrive at the east side of the library’s first floor.
cards.short_summary: A library makerspace with reservable equipment and creative-production tools.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU’s Fab Lab page lists equipment reservations, equipment in the lab, checkout equipment, and its first-floor library location.
cards.source_title: Fab Lab | TCU Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.access_notes: Check the Fab Lab’s current hours, usage policies, and reservation requirements.

cards.title: Special Collections Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.notes: Use this reading room when a class or research question calls for archival or rare material; start by checking collection guidance and asking library staff for help.
cards.short_summary: A focused research setting for TCU archives, rare books, and special collections.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU states that student researchers can use digitized resources and materials in the Special Collections reading room.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Things You Should Know About the TCU Library
cards.access_notes: Collection and reading-room handling/access procedures apply; consult library staff before a visit.

cards.title: University Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 3005 Stadium Drive
cards.notes: Choose a movement break that fits your comfort level, from courts and track to climbing or swimming, and review the live schedule and access policies first.
cards.short_summary: A large recreation facility supporting fitness, sport, climbing, and aquatic activity.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU lists the University Recreation Center’s recreation and academic space and says registered TCU students are eligible for membership.
cards.access_notes: Controlled-access facility; membership or approved access is required, and hours may change.

cards.title: Froghenge
cards.subtitle: Map-listed landmark near the Campus Commons
cards.notes: Walk over to view the stone installation, or use it as an outdoor-classroom landmark when your course or student organization has a nearby gathering.
cards.short_summary: A stone installation TCU documents as an outdoor classroom.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU says Froghenge was created by former provost Nowell Donovan and is often used as an outdoor classroom.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; use respectfully and do not interfere with scheduled instruction.

cards.title: TCU Student Memorial
cards.subtitle: Map-listed landmark on main campus
cards.notes: Pause here quietly to understand the memorial’s single-lotus design and its purpose, keeping the space suitable for reflection and remembrance.
cards.short_summary: A reflective campus memorial designed with Student Government Association involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU states that the Student Memorial was designed with the Student Government Association and honors students lost during enrollment.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial space; treat it as a place of remembrance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Free, documented TCU and Fort Worth activities; several options require a TCU or Fort Worth Public Library card.

cards.title: See the Kimbell’s permanent collection
cards.subtitle: Cultural District
cards.notes: Meet in the Kahn Building and browse the permanent collection together; keep special-exhibition galleries separate because they may require tickets.
cards.short_summary: The museum’s collection galleries are always free to enter.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Kimbell Art Museum’s collection is always free.
cards.access_notes: Free access applies to the collection; special exhibitions have separate admission.

cards.entity_name: Amon Carter Museum of American Art
cards.title: Browse the Carter galleries
cards.subtitle: Cultural District
cards.notes: Choose a gallery floor, take a slow lap through the collection, then regroup by the lobby to compare one work each.
cards.short_summary: The Carter offers free admission to its collection and special exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Amon Carter Museum of American Art states that admission is always free, including its collection and special exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Amon Carter Museum of American Art
cards.access_notes: Museum hours vary by day; check the museum’s visit page before leaving.

cards.title: Settle into a library study session
cards.subtitle: TCU campus
cards.notes: Pick a quiet-study zone or a group-study area, bring your own materials, and use the building maps to choose a floor.
cards.short_summary: TCU students can enter with ID, and visitors are welcomed during posted visitor hours.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU identifies the Mary Couts Burnett Library as student ID access and lists visitors as welcome during posted visitor hours.
cards.source_title: Alumni, Visitors and TexShare Patrons | TCU Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.access_notes: Students need a TCU ID; visitors must follow posted visitor-hour and sign-in requirements.

cards.title: Use your TCU ID for a home game
cards.subtitle: TCU campus athletic venues
cards.notes: Check the current athletics schedule, bring your TCU ID, and attend an eligible home event with classmates or friends.
cards.short_summary: TCU lists student admission to athletic events as an ID-card use.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU’s ID Center states that a TCU ID provides students free admission to athletic events.
cards.source_title: TCU ID Center | Door Card Swipe Access
cards.access_notes: For current TCU students with a valid TCU ID; confirm the event’s entry details before attending.

cards.title: Visit the BRIT building
cards.subtitle: Fort Worth Botanic Garden campus
cards.notes: Plan a weekday stop to explore the BRIT building’s public space, then use the garden map to orient yourselves nearby.
cards.short_summary: The Botanic Garden says entry to the BRIT building is always free on weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Fort Worth Botanic Garden states that entry to the BRIT building is always free Monday through Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Can I walk around the Garden before or after class? | Fort Worth Botanic Garden
cards.access_notes: Free entry is listed for Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; this does not include paid garden admission.

cards.title: Walk the Trinity Park paths
cards.subtitle: Fort Worth Cultural District
cards.notes: Start at a trail entrance, follow the paved river path at a comfortable pace, and pause at an observation deck or picnic table.
cards.short_summary: City-maintained paths connect this park with other public spaces along the Trinity River.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fort Worth describes Trinity Park as a complimentary destination with walking and bike paths along the Trinity River.
cards.source_title: Trinity Park | City of Fort Worth
cards.access_notes: Use public paths and park amenities; bring any food or equipment you want rather than relying on purchases.

cards.title: Take a foot-only prairie walk
cards.subtitle: 3400 View Street, Fort Worth
cards.notes: Walk the designated trails, look closely for native plants and insects, and leave the prairie undisturbed for the next visitors.
cards.short_summary: This protected natural area welcomes walk-in visitors and has trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fort Worth says walk-in visitors are welcome at Tandy Hills Natural Area and lists trails among its features.
cards.source_title: Tandy Hills Natural Area | City of Fort Worth
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk. Foot traffic only; stay on trails and do not collect plants, animals, or natural objects.

cards.title: Check out a Botanic Garden pass
cards.subtitle: Fort Worth Botanic Garden via Fort Worth Public Library
cards.notes: Reserve a library MusePass, follow its loan rules, and plan a general-admission garden walk on the pass’s valid visit date.
cards.short_summary: A Fort Worth Public Library card can provide free general-admission passes.
cards.evidence_claim: Fort Worth Public Library offers passes for free general admission to the Fort Worth Botanic Garden with a library card.
cards.source_title: Fort Worth Botanic Garden Passes | City of Fort Worth
cards.access_notes: Requires an available Fort Worth Public Library pass and compliance with its loan rules; excludes special events and programs.

cards.entity_name: Fort Worth Nature Center & Refuge pass
cards.title: Borrow a Nature Center pass
cards.subtitle: Fort Worth Nature Center & Refuge via Fort Worth Public Library
cards.notes: Check pass availability through the library, borrow one before the trip, and use it for a low-cost-free outdoor visit with your group.
cards.short_summary: Library cardholders can get free general admission through the city’s pass program.
cards.evidence_claim: Fort Worth Public Library states that cardholders can check out passes for free general admission to the Fort Worth Nature Center & Refuge.
cards.source_title: Nature Center Passes | City of Fort Worth
cards.access_notes: Requires an available Fort Worth Public Library pass; check the library page for current checkout details.

cards.title: Reserve a Log Cabin Village pass
cards.subtitle: Log Cabin Village via Fort Worth Public Library
cards.notes: Use a Fort Worth Public Library card to reserve a pass, then plan a self-guided visit around the village’s historic structures.
cards.short_summary: The city library’s pass program includes free access to Log Cabin Village.
cards.evidence_claim: Fort Worth Public Library states that cardholders can reserve free passes to Fort Worth’s Log Cabin Village.
cards.source_title: Oh, the places you can go! | City of Fort Worth
cards.access_notes: Requires a Fort Worth Public Library card and an available pass; verify reservation rules before planning.

cards.subtitle: Mary Couts Burnett Library · first floor

cards.evidence_claim: TCU describes the GIGA Lab as a first-floor library facility with hardware and software information and course-cleared access listings.
cards.source_title: Library Facilities: GIGA Lab | TCU Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the library’s first floor and open during library hours; consult the current cleared-course list or student request form for access.

cards.evidence_claim: Mary Couts Burnett Library offers two Media Editing Rooms for audio and video production and editing, available by reservation only.
cards.source_title: Media Editing Rooms | TCU Mary Couts Burnett Library
cards.access_notes: Reservation required; located on the library’s first floor and open during library hours.

cards.title: Special Collections Reading Room

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Horned Frog rituals, objects, and recurring celebrations that connect TCU’s campus community.

cards.title: Curl the horns
cards.subtitle: TCU school-spirit gesture
cards.notes: Make a peace sign, then curl the fingers to suggest horned-frog horns; use it as a shared TCU spirit gesture at campus events.
cards.short_summary: A curled-finger salute adopted by TCU cheerleaders and crowds in 1980.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU says cheerleader Chad Schrotel ’82 helped the Go Frogs hand sign catch on in 1980, with curled fingers representing horned-frog horns.
cards.access_notes: A public school-spirit gesture; follow event directions when participating.

cards.title: Join the Riff Ram
cards.subtitle: TCU’s century-old cheer
cards.notes: Learn the short “Riff Ram, Bah Zoo” cheer before a spirit event, then follow the crowd’s pace and cues as it builds.
cards.short_summary: TCU’s longstanding chant is paired with a repeated, quickening dance.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU describes “Riff Ram” as more than 100 years old, says it rose in the early Southwest Conference, and notes its signature dance and increasing pace.
cards.access_notes: Listen for cheerleader or event-leader cues before joining.

cards.title: Spot SuperFrog
cards.subtitle: TCU’s costumed Horned Frog mascot
cards.notes: Look for SuperFrog during a TCU athletic event and enjoy the mascot performance from the public spectator areas.
cards.short_summary: The modern mascot grew from TCU’s long sideline-mascot tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU states that costumed mascots have appeared on its football sidelines since the 1930s and that SuperFrog was created in 1979.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances depend on the event; remain in designated spectator areas.

cards.title: Rub the Lucky Frog nose
cards.subtitle: Between Sadler and Reed halls
cards.notes: Before an exam, find the pointy horned-frog statue between Sadler and Reed halls and gently rub its nose for the campus luck ritual.
cards.short_summary: A test-day superstition centered on a horned-frog statue’s nose.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU identifies rubbing the nose of the horned-frog statue between Sadler and Reed halls for test luck as a campus tradition, while noting its origin is unknown.
cards.access_notes: Visit the outdoor statue respectfully; do not climb on it or block foot traffic.

cards.title: Purple boots at Commencement
cards.subtitle: Horned Frog graduation style
cards.notes: At Commencement, watch for purple cowboy boots beneath academic regalia; if wearing your own, follow the ceremony’s published attire guidance.
cards.short_summary: Purple cowboy boots are a recognizable TCU graduation tradition with roots in the 1940s.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU says TCU boots have been seen since the 1940s and notes that stadium namesake Amon G. Carter had a pair.
cards.access_notes: Commencement attendance and attire are governed by the university’s event instructions.

cards.title: Hear the Frog Horn
cards.subtitle: Amon G. Carter Stadium touchdown ritual
cards.notes: At a home football game, listen for the large Frog Horn after a TCU touchdown and protect your hearing if you are noise-sensitive.
cards.short_summary: A 3,000-pound train horn announces Horned Frog touchdowns at home games.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU says its smoking 3,000-pound Frog Horn announces touchdowns with a blaring train horn.
cards.access_notes: Occurs at home football games after TCU touchdowns; game admission may be required.

cards.title: Start with Frogs First
cards.subtitle: TCU welcome weekend for new students
cards.notes: Eligible new students can use Frogs First to meet peers, upperclassmen, and faculty before classes begin; check the current registration details.
cards.short_summary: TCU’s new-student welcome weekend builds connections before the academic term.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU Student Activities identifies Frogs First as TCU’s welcome weekend for new students, with activities before classes that connect peers, upperclassmen, and faculty.
cards.access_notes: For incoming students; consult current university registration and schedule information.

cards.title: Gather for the Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: TCU Commons seasonal celebration
cards.notes: Check the annual schedule, then gather in the TCU Commons for the public lighting of the 50-foot Christmas tree and accompanying program.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal campus event featuring a towering lit tree, refreshments, SuperFrog Santa, and fireworks.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU Student Activities calls the Tree Lighting a time-honored tradition and lists the lighting of TCU’s 50-foot Christmas tree, refreshments, SuperFrog Santa, and fireworks.
cards.access_notes: Annual timing and attendance details vary; confirm the current Student Activities announcement.

cards.title: Watch the Rangers run flags
cards.subtitle: TCU game-day spirit team
cards.notes: From the stands, watch the TCU Rangers run flags and operate the Frog Horn as part of the home-game presentation.
cards.short_summary: The Rangers are a visible part of TCU’s football-game celebration rituals.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU lists the Rangers among its traditions and says the spirited team runs flags and the Frog Horn at games.
cards.access_notes: Watch from authorized spectator areas during a game-day event.

cards.title: Meet at Senior Sunrise
cards.subtitle: Pre-dawn gathering for graduating seniors
cards.notes: Graduating seniors can check commencement-season programming for Senior Sunrise, a before-dawn breakfast gathering to mark the end of their TCU experience.
cards.short_summary: A sunrise breakfast brings graduating seniors together in the stadium before graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: TCU describes Senior Sunrise as a tradition in which graduating seniors meet before dawn for breakfast together.
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors; verify the current ceremony-season invitation and schedule.
